output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the in-call credit limit from £100 to £25. Larger adjustments are now blocked and automatically referred to the Billing Resolution team. Billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in the week of 14 April. Referred calls resolve at about 33% and non-referred at 82%, and neither rate changed. So the drop comes from the mix shift to referrals. Experienced agents fell by the same amount as the new starters (about 75% to 67%), and referral rates are similar across tenure bands. The new starters' overall 66.4% is in line with this, so tenure isn't the cause. The tariff rise raised tariff-enquiry share, but tariff FCR is unchanged at about 85%. The IVR change came two weeks after the drop, so it doesn't explain it. Complaints rose, but that link is only loosely shown: the log is mostly uncategorised and isn't tied to calls. I did not test workload directly, so that view is weakly held. Don't put the April intake on performance plans. Instead, agree a revised credit limit with Finance, backed by post-call sampling of credits. Trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and unsupported credits. Finance has said it would consider this. MI can rerun the breakdown for those teams within a day, so the rebuilt dashboard can wait.
